payload.reason: The evidence indicates that in the UCCA scheme, a node can represent either a terminal or multiple terminals as a single entity, suggesting that a node can be both types depending on the context.

claims.text: A node in the UCCA scheme can be either a terminal or a non-terminal, but not both simultaneously.
UCCA nodes can represent multiple terminals viewed as a single entity, indicating flexibility in node classification.
Non-terminal nodes in UCCA represent units comprising more than one word, supporting the idea of nodes being non-terminal.
